Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

openalexConvert 0.1.1

  • License changed from GPL (>= 2) to MIT.
  • corpus_to_csljson() wrote every item’s publication date as an empty "issued": {"date-parts": []}: the internal sanitizer only kept named list elements, so the unnamed date-parts list was emptied. All dates were lost in the CSL JSON and in everything converted from it (BibTeX/BibLaTeX had no usable year, citations showed “n.d.”). Dates are now written.
  • corpus_to_csljson() treated a missing (NA) ISBN or ISSN-L as present, because nzchar(NA) is TRUE. As a result every book and preprint was written as article-journal, and the ISSN never fell back to the work’s list of ISSNs when the ISSN-L was missing. Books now stay book, preprints become manuscript, and the ISSN fallback works.
  • corpus_to_csljson() wrote OA_status:NA into the note (and so into Zotero’s Extra field) for works without an open-access status. A missing status is now left out.
  • csljson_to_zotero(): when Zotero refused to create a collection or to grant write access with a plain-text error (e.g. Forbidden), the response was parsed as JSON before its status was checked, so the user saw an unhelpful jsonlite “lexical error” instead of the intended message. The status is now checked first.

openalexConvert 0.1.0

Zotero import rewritten

csljson_to_zotero_upload() is removed. It POSTed CSL JSON to the Zotero Web API, which only accepts Zotero item JSON and at most 50 items per request, so real uploads could not succeed; its tests only exercised mocked responses.

New csljson_to_zotero(files, method = c("local", "web")):

  • method = "local" imports CSL JSON files (e.g. the chunks from corpus_to_csljson()) into the running Zotero desktop app via its local connector endpoint. Zotero’s own CSL JSON importer does the mapping, and items go into the library or collection selected in Zotero; select a group library to import into the group. Verified against Zotero 10.0.6.
  • Each item’s OpenAlex ID ends up in Zotero’s Extra field as OpenAlex: W... (see below).
  • Re-exports: existing = c("skip", "update", "overwrite") decides what happens to items whose OpenAlex ID is already in the selected Zotero library. "skip" (default) leaves them alone; "update" writes the new metadata but keeps fields it lacks; "overwrite" replaces all fields and empties those it lacks. Both keep the Zotero item key, notes, attachments, tags and collections. They need Zotero 10’s local API and a one-time “Always Allow” in Zotero.
  • Existing items are recognised whichever form their Extra uses for the ID: OpenAlex: W... (written by this package), OpenAlex: https://openalex.org/W... (Zotero’s OpenAlex translators), openalex.work_id: W... (zotero-openalex plugin) or OpenAlex Work ID: W... (open-alex-work-id plugin).
  • corpus_to_zotero(project_dir) does both steps in one call: corpus to temporary CSL JSON (1000 works per file) to Zotero, into the collection <project> > <corpus>.
  • Collections: csljson_to_zotero(collection = c("project", "corpus")) puts the works into a nested collection, created if missing and reused on re-export. Works already in the library join it too, whatever existing says. corpus_to_zotero() does this by default, naming the collections after the project directory and the corpus, so an accidental export is easy to find and delete.
  • Tags: csljson_to_zotero(tags = ) and corpus_to_zotero() write tags by OpenAlex ID (e.g. from zotero_tags.parquet, which corpus_to_zotero() picks up from the project directory). New items get their tags; existing items follow existing: "skip" leaves them alone, "update" adds missing tags, "overwrite" replaces them. New result column n_tagged.
  • method = "web" (headless upload via the Zotero Web API) is not implemented yet and raises an error.
  • The help page’s “Speed” section gives measured import times: Zotero slows as the library grows (17.5 works/s at 440 items, 6.1 works/s at 4440), so 100000 works take hours.

OpenAlex ID in the CSL note

corpus_to_csljson() now writes note as lines, the first being OpenAlex: W... (followed by the existing OA:...; OA_status:...; Citations:... line). Zotero imports note into Extra, so the ID is kept however the CSL JSON reaches Zotero, including File → Import. The CSL test fixtures were regenerated; only note changed. BibTeX/BibLaTeX output is unchanged (pandoc does not write note).

Zotero tags back into the project

New zotero_tags(project_dir) reads the tags of every item in the Zotero library selected in Zotero that has an OpenAlex ID in Extra (any of the four forms) and writes them to zotero_tags.parquet in the project directory: one row per work and tag, with the tag type (manual/automatic), the library (group ID, 0 = personal library) and the Zotero item key. Join it with the corpus on openalex_id. Re-running replaces that library’s rows and keeps those of other libraries. Reading needs no API key.

DuckDB lambda syntax

corpus_to_csljson() failed with current DuckDB (“Deprecated lambda arrow (->) detected”). It now uses the lambda x: ... syntax.

openalexConvert 0.0.5

Tests no longer compare pandoc’s exact output

Every r-universe check failed — Linux, macOS and Windows, all R versions — in test-001-corpus_csl_pandoc.R:

actual (r-universe):  year = {0000}
expected (fixture):   year = {0000},
                      doi = {10.1163/9789004190351_002}

r-universe builds with pandoc 3.9, which omits doi = {...} for these entry types; the fixtures had been regenerated in 0.0.4 on a machine with pandoc 3.12, which writes it. Same input, same code, different pandoc.

Those five comparisons were guarded by skip_on_ci(), which GitHub Actions honours — so CI stayed green — but r-universe does not set CI, so they ran there.

Byte-comparing pandoc’s output tests pandoc, not this package. The tests now compare what csljson_convert_pandoc() is actually responsible for: that every record in comes out. BibTeX and BibLaTeX compare citation keys, LaTeX compares the OpenAlex ids carried in \bibitem, and the markdown test keeps its structural assertions (markdown renders citations as author-year text, so no ids survive to match on).

The skip_on_ci() guards are gone with them, so these five now run on every platform instead of being skipped on CI.

openalexConvert 0.0.4

Require openalexPro (>= 0.11.0)

.normalize_doi() delegates to openalexPro::extract_doi(normalize = TRUE) (R/corpus_to_csljson.R:430), and before openalexPro 0.11.0 that function silently truncated DOIs containing <, >, [ or ] – returning a shorter string that still looked like a valid DOI, with no warning and no NA. Roughly 0.38% of real DOIs are affected (SICI-style ones, common in older journal content).

The dependency carried no version floor, so installing against an older openalexPro produced quietly corrupted DOIs in the CSL-JSON output.

Fixtures regenerated: they encoded the truncation bug

Once the floor was in place the suite failed, because every comparison fixture had been recorded while extract_doi() was still truncating. The fixtures expected the wrong answer:

generated: "10.1659/0276-4741(2005)025[0206:pfbcs]2.0.co;2"   <- correct
fixture:   "10.1659/0276-4741(2005)025"                       <- truncated

The BibTeX and BibLaTeX fixtures were stale in a second way: entries whose DOI had been lost now carry a doi = {...} field they previously lacked.

Every difference was verified to be DOI-related before regenerating – 6 differing CSL fields and 187 differing .bib lines, all of them a DOI value or a doi = line (plus the trailing comma that appears on the line above a newly added field). Nothing else moved.

data-raw/regenerate_fixtures.R now does this reproducibly, and refuses to run outside a UTF-8 locale: in a C locale R renders non-ASCII author names as literal <U+00F3> escapes and pandoc writes Bay\textless U+00F3\textgreater n into the .bib files, which is exactly how a broken fixture gets committed and then becomes the expectation.

The suite now passes: 119 pass / 0 fail, from 105 pass / 14 fail.

openalexConvert 0.0.3

Bug fixes

  • corpus_export_via_pandoc(): now produces a single output file (e.g. corpus.bib) as documented. Previously it passed the chunked CSL JSON directory to csljson_convert_pandoc(), which created a directory of per-chunk files at the output path, and it returned the wrong path when an extension had to be appended.
  • csljson_convert_pandoc(): the pdf_engine parameter is now respected. Previously --pdf-engine=xelatex was unconditionally appended, overriding any user-specified engine (e.g. "lualatex" or "pdflatex").
  • DOI extraction now delegates to openalexPro::extract_doi(), which fixes a regex that missed lowercase characters in DOI suffixes (e.g. 10.1234/abc-def).

Improvements

  • openalexPro declared as a formal dependency in DESCRIPTION (Imports).
  • rmarkdown moved from Suggests to Imports (it is used in exported functions).
  • Additional_repositories added to DESCRIPTION so CI and users can resolve openalexPro from r-universe automatically.
  • CI aligned with the rest of the openalexPro ecosystem: standard R-CMD-check.yaml (macOS, Windows, Ubuntu × devel/release/oldrel-1) and test-coverage.yaml added.
  • Test coverage raised to ~86%, with new tests for corpus_export_via_pandoc(), Pandoc rendering paths, and csljson_to_zotero_upload().
  • Leftover _problems/ test artefacts from a previous failed run removed.
